title: LUTein: Dense-Sparse Bit-Slice Architecture With Radix-4 LUT-Based Slice-Tensor Processing Units
problem: Bit-slice architectures face power trade-offs in multiplier design that cannot efficiently handle all data sparsity ranges, and existing core architectures focus on either dense or sparse computations exclusively, not both. Additionally, low-bit computations cause massive repetitive instruction fetches and large data transactions in conventional PE designs.
motivation: Supporting variable bit-precision and data sparsity in DNNs is essential for energy-efficient inference, but existing bit-slice architectures cannot simultaneously optimize for the full range of sparsity patterns.
method: LUTein uses look-up tables (precomputed hardware results) with the Radix-4 Modified Booth multiplication algorithm to keep power consumption low whether data is dense (full of values) or sparse (mostly zeros). Its processing elements share hardware resources, reducing data movement between different parts of the chip. The architecture arranges data flow in a systolic pattern (a pipeline where data moves in waves) and uses multiple buffers to let processing units reuse each other's data and recognize when sections of computation involve all zeros. A specialized instruction decoder minimizes how often instructions need to be fetched, preventing that from becoming a bottleneck.
key_novelty: The core idea is combining look-up-table-based multiplication with the Radix-4 Modified Booth algorithm to maintain low power across all data sparsity ranges, enabling a single unified architecture for both dense and sparse computations.
contributions: LUT-based Radix-4 Modified Booth multiplier supporting efficient computation across full sparsity spectrum
Slice-tensor PE architecture with shared hardware units for reduced data transactions
Systolic datapath with multi-port buffer for inter-PE data reuse and sparsity exploitation
Hierarchical instruction decoder and ISA to reduce repetitive instruction fetch overhead
limitations: Limitations, scalability beyond DNNs, and comparison scope not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: Efficient bit-slice DNN accelerator with LUT-based sparsity-aware processing
